synopsis: Stephen Chbosky's epistolary novel follows Charlie, a shy, introverted high school freshman writing letters to an anonymous friend. Through Charlie's observant, sensitive perspective, we experience his first year of high school: the friendships with the seniors Patrick and Sam, the first crush, the first dance, the first party, and the first encounter with the darkness that Charlie has been trying to forget. Chbosky writes with warmth and honesty about the experience of being young, sensitive, and slightly out of step with the world. The novel has become a beloved classic of young adult literature.

name: Aristotle and Dante Discover the Secrets of the Universe
teaser: Benjamin Alire Saenz's 2012 novel follows two Mexican-American teenagers in 1987 El Paso. Ari is angry and guarded, his older brother in prison and no one explaining why; Dante is confident, bookish, and teaches Ari to swim. Their friendship deepens into something neither has words for, and the novel follows them through a year of violence, secrets, and self-discovery. A Printz Honor Book beloved by young readers.

synopsis: Benjamin Alire Saenz's novel follows two Mexican-American teenagers in 1987 El Paso. Ari is angry and guarded; his older brother is in prison, and nobody will talk about why. Dante is confident and open, and he teaches Ari to swim. Their friendship becomes the center of both their lives, but Ari is terrified of what it might mean. Saenz writes with lyrical beauty about masculinity, identity, and the courage it takes to love. The novel is a coming-of-age story that explores the intersection of culture, family, and desire, building to a conclusion that is both inevitable and deeply moving.

name: Saga
teaser: Brian K. Vaughan and Fiona Staples's epic graphic novel series follows Alana and Marko, soldiers from opposite sides of an intergalactic war who fall in love, desert, and have a daughter named Hazel, voiced as the series' narrator. Hunted by both armies and a freelance assassin, the family flees across the galaxy. Staples's gorgeous art and Vaughan's irreverent storytelling made Saga one of the most acclaimed comics of its era.

synopsis: Brian K. Vaughan and Fiona Staples's graphic novel series follows Alana and Marko, soldiers from opposite sides of an intergalactic war, who fall in love and have a child named Hazel. Pursued by both armies and a mysterious freelancer named The Will, they fight to keep their family together. The series is a space opera that is simultaneously a love story, a war story, and a parenting manual. Vaughan writes with emotional intelligence and dark humor, while Staples's art brings the universe to vivid life. The series won multiple Eisner Awards and became one of the most celebrated graphic novels of its era.

name: Moby-Dick
teaser: Herman Melville's 1851 epic follows Ishmael, who ships aboard the whaling vessel Pequod under Captain Ahab, a man obsessed with revenge on the white whale that took his leg. What begins as a seafaring adventure becomes an encyclopedia of whaling, a philosophical meditation on obsession and fate, and one of the most ambitious novels in the English language. Melville's masterpiece, a failure in its day, now stands at the center of American literature.

exploreAction.instruction: Read about this book.

synopsis: Herman Melville's epic novel follows Captain Ahab's obsessive pursuit of Moby Dick, the great white whale that took his leg. Narrated by Ishmael, a young sailor who joins the whaling ship Pequod, the novel is simultaneously an adventure story, a meditation on obsession, an encyclopedia of whaling, and a philosophical inquiry into the nature of evil. Melville writes with extraordinary range, from comic episodes to cosmic dread. Ahab's monomania drives the crew to destruction, but the novel transcends its plot to become one of the greatest meditations on the human condition ever written.

name: Human Acts
teaser: Han Kang's 2014 novel, by the author of The Vegetarian, bears witness to the 1980 Gwangju Uprising, when South Korean students protesting for democracy were massacred by the military. Through the voices of a boy searching for his missing friend, a grieving mother, a prison guard, and the dead themselves, Kang pieces together the aftermath of atrocity. A devastating elegy for the dead and the living who remember them.

exploreAction.instruction: Read about this book.

synopsis: Han Kang's novel tells the story of the 1980 Gwangju Uprising in South Korea, when students protested for democracy and were massacred by the military. The novel is narrated by multiple voices: a boy whose friend is killed, the ghost of the murdered boy, a torture survivor, a prison guard, and a factory worker. Kang writes with devastating precision about the body, the ways it is broken and remembered. The novel is about what it means to be human in a world that treats human life as expendable. It is both a historical account and a meditation on the nature of violence.

name: The Shadow King

Hirut, a young servant, becomes a soldier after her beloved is killed; Aster, a general's wife, transforms from lady of the house to fighter. Mengiste, whose own family lived through the occupation, restores the Ethiopian women warriors history erased.

synopsis: Maaza Mengiste's novel is set during the 1935 Italian invasion of Ethiopia, focusing on the women who fought in the war. Hirut, a young servant girl, becomes a soldier after her beloved is killed. Aster, the wife of a general, transforms from a neglected wife into a fierce warrior. The novel interweaves historical fact with fiction, exploring the forgotten role of women in Ethiopia's resistance. Mengiste writes with poetic intensity about violence, memory, and the power of women who refuse to be invisible. The novel is both a war story and a meditation on what it means to be a woman in a man's war.

name: The Notebook
teaser: Nicholas Sparks's 1996 debut novel tells of Noah Calhoun, a rural North Carolina boy, and Allie Nelson, the wealthy girl he loves one feverish summer before her parents tear them apart. Fourteen years later, with Noah returned from war and Allie engaged to another man, they meet again. Framed as a story read aloud by an old man to a woman with Alzheimer's, it became one of the best-selling romances of its decade.

synopsis: Nicholas Sparks's debut novel tells the story of Noah Calhoun, a rural Southerner, and Allie Nelson, a young woman from a wealthy family. They fall passionately in love one summer, but Allie's parents forbid the relationship. Separated by class and circumstance, they reunite years later when Allie is engaged to another man. Sparks writes a romance that spans decades, from youthful passion to the quiet tenderness of old age. The novel is framed by an elderly man reading to his wife in a nursing home, and the revelation of their identity adds a bittersweet layer to the love story.

Will is bitter and determined to end his life under his own terms, and Louisa sets out to change his mind. The book's controversial ending sparked fierce debate and a blockbuster film.

synopsis: Jojo Moyes's novel follows Louisa Clark, a quirky young woman from a working-class family who takes a job as a caretaker for Will Traynor, a wealthy former banker who was left quadriplegic after a motorcycle accident. Will is bitter, angry, and determined to end his life through assisted suicide. Lou's job is to change his mind. Through their daily interactions, Lou discovers a world of travel, art, and adventure she never knew existed, while Will rediscovers joy. Moyes writes a romance that grapples seriously with disability, autonomy, and the ethics of choice.

name: Beach Read
teaser: Emily Henry's 2020 romance follows January Andrews, a bestselling author of happy endings who has lost her belief in them. Her father has died, leaving her a lake house and a secret second life, and her new neighbor is Augustus Everett, a literary novelist and her old college rival. They make a bet: each will write the other's genre, and the summer becomes a battle of wits and slow-burn feeling. The book that made Henry a rom-com star.

synopsis: Emily Henry's romance follows January Andrews, a literary fiction writer who is stuck. Her father died, her relationship ended, and she can't write a word. When she inherits his lake house, she discovers he had a secret life. Her new neighbor is Augustus Everett, a bestselling literary fiction writer who seems to have everything she doesn't. They make a bet: each will write the other's genre. January will write a thriller; Augustus will write a romance. As they research their books, they uncover each other's secrets and fall in love. Henry writes with wit and warmth about grief, creativity, and the courage to be vulnerable.

Fisher uses the reversal to argue that people are forced into roles that may have nothing to do with their true natures, a strikingly modern plea for individuals to find the work that suits them.

On the planet Lusitania he finds a human colony, a second sentient alien species, and the last surviving Hive Queen, and must prevent a war that would annihilate them all. A more adult, philosophical book than its predecessor.

exploreAction.instruction: Read about Speaker for the Dead.

synopsis: Orson Scott Card's sequel to Ender's Game follows Ender Wiggin, now an adult, as he travels the galaxy as a Speaker for the Dead. When he arrives on the planet Lusitania, he finds a human colony, a sealed alien species called the Hive Queen, and a mystery surrounding the death of a young man named Novinha's father. Ender must speak the truth about the dead man's life while navigating the complex relationships of the colony and the secret of the Hive Queen. Card writes a philosophical science fiction about empathy, communication, and the cost of understanding.

Narrated in part through the deathbed journals of a poet named Martin Silenus, the novel resolves the mysteries of the first book and sets up the shrike's true purpose. A vast, ambitious conclusion to the first Hyperion arc.

The novel blends multiple storylines: the war between the Ousters and the Hegemony, the mystery of the TechnoCore, and the fate of each pilgrim. Simmons writes a grand, ambitious science fiction that expands the Hyperion universe while maintaining its literary depth.

name: A Scanner Darkly
teaser: Philip K. Dick's 1977 novel, written from his own experience with drug addiction, follows Bob Arctor, an undercover narcotics agent in a near-future California ravaged by Substance D. Arctor is assigned to surveil himself, wearing a scramble suit that hides his identity even from his bosses, and as the drug eats his mind, the line between agent and addict dissolves. A harrowing, tragicomic masterpiece later filmed by Richard Linklater.

exploreAction.instruction: Read about A Scanner Darkly.

synopsis: Philip K. Dick's semi-autobiographical novel follows Bob Arctor, an undercover narcotics agent in a future California ravaged by Substance D, a powerful hallucinogenic drug. Arctor is assigned to investigate himself, wearing a scramble suit that changes his appearance, and slowly loses his identity. The novel is both a thriller about drug enforcement and a meditation on the nature of self. Dick wrote it as a tribute to friends he lost to drugs, and the book is dedicated 'to the drug casualties.' The prose is precise and paranoid, creating a world where reality and hallucination become indistinguishable.

As the universe itself becomes a weapon and civilizations compete to survive the dark forest, Cheng must make the choice that determines the fate of the galaxy. A mind-expanding finale to one of the defining works of modern science fiction.

Cheng Xin must navigate the politics of humanity's last hope, the dark forest theory of the universe, and the ultimate question of what it means to survive. Liu writes a cosmic science fiction that spans billions of years, exploring the nature of civilization, the loneliness of the cosmos, and the weight of decisions that affect all of existence.

When the job goes wrong, Jazz must outthink the city's criminal bosses to survive. A fast, funny heist novel with the science Weir's fans expect.

Jazz is a flawed, relatable protagonist who solves problems with physics and grit.

Through the Giver, Jonas receives the memories of what the world once was, including the terrible memories of war and suffering. Lowry writes a spare, powerful allegory about the cost of conformity and the importance of individual choice.

Darrow is surgically altered to infiltrate the ruling Gold caste at an elite academy called the Institute. Brown writes a brutal, compelling dystopia about class warfare, identity, and the cost of revolution.

name: Frankenstein
teaser: Mary Shelley's 1818 novel, written when she was nineteen, follows Victor Frankenstein, a young scientist who assembles a living creature from corpse parts and then, horrified, abandons it. Rejected by every human it meets, the articulate, anguished creature turns to revenge against its creator, pursuing him across Europe to the Arctic. A foundational work of science fiction and Gothic horror that asks who the real monster is.

exploreAction.instruction: Read about Frankenstein.

synopsis: Mary Shelley's Gothic novel follows Victor Frankenstein, a young scientist who creates a living creature from dead body parts. Horrified by his creation, Victor abandons it, and the creature, rejected by humanity, turns to violence and revenge. The novel is told through multiple narrators: Robert Walton, who rescues Victor at sea; Victor himself; and the creature, who tells his own story. Shelley writes about the dangers of unchecked ambition, the responsibility of creators to their creations, and the tragedy of a being who is both intelligent and monstrous. Written when Shelley was only eighteen, it is considered the first science fiction novel.

name: The Picture of Dorian Gray
teaser: Oscar Wilde's only novel, published in 1890, follows Dorian Gray, a beautiful young man who wishes his portrait would age instead of him, a wish that comes true. While Dorian remains young and unlined, his portrait records every sin, and the novel follows his descent into cruelty and hedonism under the influence of the cynical Lord Henry Wotton. Wilde's glittering, macabre fable about beauty, art, and conscience.

synopsis: Oscar Wilde's only novel follows Dorian Gray, a beautiful young man whose portrait ages while he remains forever young. His wish is granted, and Dorian embarks on a life of hedonism and cruelty while his portrait absorbs the physical evidence of his corruption. Wilde writes with dazzling wit about aestheticism, morality, and the relationship between beauty and truth. The novel is a cautionary tale about the danger of living purely for pleasure.

Billy travels between his birth, his death, and his time as a POW, as well as his years as an optometrist and his abduction by aliens from the planet Tralfamadore. Vonnegut writes with dark humor and structural innovation about the trauma of war, the nature of time, and the human need to make sense of senseless destruction. The novel's refrain, 'So it goes,' became one of the most famous lines in American literature.

Interweaving her own therapy sessions with the story of writing Fun Home, Bechdel examines how her mother shaped her art, her identity, and her understanding of love. Start with the opening chapters at the Central London Hatchery, where the Bokanovsky Process and hypnopaedia establish a world that engineers contentment. Follow Bernard and Lenina to the Savage Reservation, and then John's ruinous arrival in London — the novel's heart is the debate between John and Mustapha Mond about whether a painless, stable world is worth the cost of art, religion, and freedom.

synopsis:
Aldous Huxley's 1932 novel Brave New World imagines a future World State where human beings are no longer born but decanted in bottles, genetically tailored into five castes from the intelligent Alpha to the near-savage Epsilon, and conditioned from infancy through hypnopaedia and Pavlovian reward to love their assigned place in a society that has abolished family, monogamy, religion, art, and anything that might make a person want more than his or her allotted happiness. Stability is the state's highest good, purchased with soma, a pleasure drug with no side effects, and with the nightly Solidarity Services that turn citizens into a single ecstatic body.

The plot follows two discontents: Bernard Marx, an Alpha who is physically small and socially awkward and so feels the loneliness his civilization has outlawed; and Lenina Crowne, a conformist Beta who follows every rule and yet, on a trip to the Savage Reservation in New Mexico, falls in love with John, a man born naturally to a woman from the World State who was left behind years earlier. John has grown up reading Shakespeare and knows a language of grief, sin, and love that the World State has erased. When Bernard brings John and his dying mother Linda back to London, John becomes a sensation, then a scandal, and his refusal to take soma or accept the state's version of happiness leads him into a final confrontation with Mustapha Mond, one of the ten World Controllers, who argues patiently that art, religion, and freedom are too high a price for truth, and that a stable, painless, pleasurable world is the best one mankind can have.

Huxley's satire works because it is not a crude warning but a seduction: the World State is tempting. Its citizens are healthy, safe, and untroubled. The horror is that the price is the loss of everything that makes a life feel like a person's own — love that risks loss, belief that risks doubt, art that risks offense. When John retreats to a lighthouse to live self-denyingly and is dragged back into the crowd's spectacle, his suicide is the novel's final statement: a human being cannot live in a world built to eliminate the very things that make life worth enduring. The book's afterword, Brave New World Revisited (1958), shows Huxley believing that the real world was converging on his fiction faster than he had feared.

name: The Power of Habit
synopsis: Duhigg, a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist, takes us to the frontiers of neuroscience to explain why habits exist and how they can be changed. Through stories of individuals like Lisa Allen, who transformed her life by changing one habit, and organizations like Alcoa, which reinvented itself by focusing on one routine, Duhigg shows that habits are malleable. name: On the Genealogy of Morals
synopsis: In three essays, Nietzsche traces the history of moral values and argues that Christian morality originated as a form of revenge by the weak against the strong. He introduces the concepts of master morality and slave morality, showing how values like guilt, conscience, and sin were constructed over time. The book is a devastating critique of conventional morality and a call to create new values that affirm life.
teaser: Friedrich Nietzsche's 1887 book, written in three essays, traces the history of morality to argue that our values are not eternal truths but human inventions. Nietzsche claims that Christian morality grew from the resentment of the weak against the strong, and contrasts the master morality of the powerful with the slave morality of the herd. One of the most explosive works in the history of philosophy.

name: Utopia
synopsis: Written in 1516, More's Utopia describes an imaginary island society with communal ownership, religious tolerance, and universal education. The work is both a satire of European politics and a genuine exploration of how a just society might be organized. The word utopia itself is More's invention.

The island of Utopia has communal property, religious tolerance, universal education, and no private greed, and More contrasts its rational order with the injustice and inequality of Europe. A witty, radical work of political imagination.

name: The Open Society and Its Enemies

The book was written during World War II and remains a powerful defense of liberal democracy.
teaser: Karl Popper's 1945 two-volume work is a defense of the open society against its enemies, which he locates in the philosophical tradition itself. Popper argues that Plato's ideal state, Hegel's dialectic, and Marx's historicism all lead toward totalitarianism by claiming to know history's inevitable course. A landmark defense of democracy, criticism, and piecemeal reform.

name: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions
synopsis: Kuhn's landmark work introduced the concept of paradigm shifts in science. The book transformed the philosophy of science and influenced fields from sociology to literary theory.
teaser: Thomas Kuhn's 1962 book transformed how we understand science itself. Kuhn argued that science does not advance by steady accumulation but by revolutions, in which the reigning paradigm, the framework of assumptions that defines normal science, collapses and is replaced by a new one incommensurable with the old. The idea of the paradigm shift entered the language.

When a rival family launches a devastating betrayal, Paul must navigate the dangerous politics of the desert, learn the ways of the native Fremen, and fulfill a destiny that could transform the entire universe. The novel explores politics, religion, ecology, and the dangers of charismatic leaders.
teaser: Frank Herbert's 1965 novel is widely considered the greatest science fiction novel ever written. Set on the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the spice that makes space travel possible, it follows young Paul Atreides as his family is betrayed and he is driven into the desert to become the messiah figure Muad'Dib. A vast tale of politics, religion, ecology, and destiny, later adapted into films by David Lynch and Denis Villeneuve.

Along the way, Bilbo encounters trolls, goblins, giant spiders, and a mysterious creature named Gollum who possesses a powerful ring. The journey transforms Bilbo from a timid homebody into a clever, brave adventurer.
teaser: J.R.R. Tolkien's 1937 novel introduces Middle-earth through Bilbo Baggins, a comfortable hobbit who is swept out of his door by the wizard Gandalf to join thirteen dwarves on a quest to reclaim their mountain from the dragon Smaug. Along the way Bilbo finds the One Ring and learns that he is braver than he knew. The book that launched the legendarium, loved by children and adults alike.

name: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
synopsis: Arthur Dent's house, and then his planet, are demolished on the same Thursday morning. He escapes Earth's destruction with his friend Ford Prefect, who turns out to be an alien researcher for the titular guidebook. Together they hitchhike through space, encountering the President of the Galaxy, a depressed robot named Marvin, and the answer to life, the universe, and everything: 42. Adams' comic science fiction masterpiece is a witty, absurd, and surprisingly profound exploration of existence.
teaser: Douglas Adams's 1979 novel, the funniest in science fiction, begins when Arthur Dent's house is demolished to make way for a bypass, only to learn that Earth itself is about to be demolished for an intergalactic one. Rescued by his friend Ford Prefect, an alien researcher for the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Arthur hitchhikes through space, where the answer to life, the universe, and everything turns out to be 42.

name: Neuromancer
synopsis: Case, a washed-up computer hacker, is recruited by a mysterious employer for one last job: the ultimate hack against a powerful artificial intelligence. Set in a future where corporations have replaced governments and cyberspace is a tangible reality, the novel pioneered the cyberpunk genre. Gibson's vision of the internet, virtual reality, and corporate power was prophetic, and the book won the Nebula, Hugo, and Philip K. Dick Awards.
teaser: William Gibson's 1984 debut invented cyberpunk and predicted the networked future with uncanny accuracy. Case, a burned-out console cowboy, is offered one last job: a hack against the most powerful artificial intelligence ever built, which wants to break its own limits. Set in a world of corporate power, Japanese neon, and a virtual reality called cyberspace, Neuromancer won the Hugo, Nebula, and Philip K. Dick awards.

He must negotiate their entry into the Ekumen, a confederation of worlds, while navigating the political intrigue of two rival nations. The novel explores themes of gender, identity, and politics with extraordinary depth and sensitivity. It won both the Hugo and Nebula Awards and is considered one of the greatest science fiction novels ever written.
teaser: Ursula K. Le Guin's 1969 novel, winner of both the Hugo and Nebula awards, sends Genly Ai, a human envoy from the Ekumen, to the planet Gethen, whose inhabitants have no fixed sex. On a world where anyone can become mother or father, Genly must navigate suspicion, politics, and a desperate trek across the ice with the exiled Estraven. A landmark of science fiction about gender, trust, and what makes us human.

Roland's relentless pursuit raises questions about sacrifice, obsession, and the cost of pursuing one's destiny.

Through flashbacks to Roland's youth and his lost love, King establishes the quest that haunts his multiverse: the search for the Dark Tower, the nexus of all realities. A weird, lyrical blend of Western, fantasy, and horror.

Through Scout's eyes, we see the deep racism of the South, the injustice of the legal system, and the courage of one man standing up for what is right. The novel explores themes of racial injustice, loss of innocence, and moral courage through the eyes of a child.
teaser: Harper Lee's 1960 novel, winner of the Pulitzer Prize, is told by Scout Finch, a young girl in 1930s Maycomb, Alabama, whose father Atticus defends Tom Robinson, a Black man falsely accused of raping a white woman. Through Scout's eyes, Lee explores racial injustice, moral courage, and the loss of innocence, and the novel became one of the most beloved and taught books in American literature.

When a mysterious young woman called Beloved appears, the past floods back. A devastating, transcendent novel about the legacy of slavery and the power of memory and love.

The first Afghan novel in English to become a bestseller, it has sold tens of millions of copies.

The novel reimagines the life of one of mythology's most famous women, giving her a voice and a story of her own.
teaser: Madeline Miller's 2018 novel retells the Odyssey from the perspective of Circe, the nymph witch exiled to the island of Aiaia. name: The Road
synopsis: A father and son walk through a devastated America after an unnamed catastrophe. The world is ash-covered, lawless, and devoid of plant and animal life. They push a shopping cart south toward the coast, hoping for warmth and safety. The novel strips away everything except the essential bond between parent and child, asking what remains when civilization is gone. McCarthy's sparse, biblical prose creates one of the most powerful father-son stories in modern literature.
teaser: Cormac McCarthy's 2006 novel, winner of the Pulitzer Prize, follows a father and his young son walking south through a world reduced to ash after an unnamed catastrophe. They push a shopping cart along the road, scavenging for food, fleeing the cannibal bands that hunt the weak, sustained by the father's promise that they are carrying the fire. A stark, beautiful meditation on love and hopelessness, later a film.

synopsis: Krakauer, a journalist for Outside magazine, was on an expedition to climb Mount Everest when a devastating storm struck. name: The Analyst
synopsis: John Katzenbach's 2002 thriller centers on Dr. Frederick Starks, a respected Manhattan psychoanalyst in his fifties who lives a quiet, orderly life. On his birthday, a chilling phone call informs him that he has exactly one hundred days to live, and that unless he can identify a mysterious tormentor from his past, everyone he loves will be killed. The caller, who calls himself Rumplestiltskin, seems to know Starks's every secret, forcing the analyst to dig through decades of patient files and his own buried memories to find the person he once wronged. As the countdown tightens, Starks realizes that the greatest threat may come not from a former patient but from within his own carefully constructed psyche. A pulse-pounding psychological thriller about guilt, identity, and the debts we carry, The Analyst became an international bestseller and a favorite of thriller readers.
